title: Add upgrade-safe persistent storage, real Excel import/export, and production deployment workflow

requirements.text: Implement upgrade-safe persistent storage in the Motoko backend so that forms, dropdown options, reports, entities, import history, and authorization state survive canister upgrades and restarts.
acceptanceCriteria: After creating forms/dropdowns/reports/entities and updating import status, redeploying/upgrading the canister retains all previously stored data.
Authorization/admin bootstrap state remains intact after upgrade (no unintended role reset).
No breaking changes to existing frontend calls (existing methods still work as before).

requirements.text: If required by the existing project’s upgrade path, add/modify backend upgrade hooks (and create backend/migration.mo only if necessary) to safely migrate existing in-memory data into stable storage during upgrade and restore it after upgrade.
acceptanceCriteria: Upgrading from the current version to the new version does not trap and results in correct restored data structures.
A clear, minimal migration strategy is present only if needed to preserve old state (no unnecessary migration file added).

requirements.text: Replace the placeholder Excel workflow UI with functional Excel template generation: allow users to select a form and download an .xlsx template whose columns are derived from the selected form’s fields, including an instructions sheet in the workbook.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking “Download Template” downloads a valid .xlsx file (not an alert) for the selected form.
The template includes a header row that matches the form field names (and/or display labels) in a consistent, documented way.
The workbook includes a second sheet with plain-English instructions for how to fill the template.

requirements.text: Implement real Excel import: allow users to upload a filled .xlsx file, parse it client-side, validate rows against the selected form definition (required fields, field types), show a preview of valid/invalid rows with error messages, and then import valid rows into the backend as entity records.
acceptanceCriteria: Uploading an .xlsx file produces a parsed preview (no placeholder alerts) showing row-level validation results.
User can confirm import of valid rows; imported rows appear in the relevant module list (students/enquiries/fees/attendance or the selected form’s entities).
Invalid rows are not imported and display clear error messages referencing the row and the problematic column/field.
The backend records import status in import history so the existing import status queries reflect the latest import summary.

requirements.text: Implement real Excel export: allow users to export existing records for a selected form to a downloadable .xlsx file with a consistent column order based on the form definition and include basic metadata columns when appropriate (e.g., record id, createdAt).
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking “Export to Excel” downloads a valid .xlsx file (not an alert) containing the selected data.
Exported rows match the current backend records for the selected form.
The exported file opens cleanly in Excel/LibreOffice with readable headers.

requirements.text: Add any necessary backend APIs to support bulk import efficiently (e.g., a bulk create endpoint and a structured response), while keeping existing single-record create and list APIs working unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: There is a backend method suitable for importing many rows in one request for a given form.
The bulk import method enforces the same authorization rules as existing entity creation (users must be authorized).
The bulk import method returns enough information for the frontend to display a summary (counts and per-row errors if applicable).

requirements.text: Provide a production deployment workflow for the Internet Computer: document and verify the steps to build and deploy the frontend and backend to the IC mainnet, including required environment variables (e.g., CAFFEINE_ADMIN_TOKEN) and post-deploy verification steps.
acceptanceCriteria: A written production deployment guide exists in-repo (English), covering: prerequisites, `dfx deploy --network ic`, environment variables, admin bootstrap token usage, and how to obtain/open the deployed frontend canister URL.
Following the guide results in a working deployed app where a user can log in via Internet Identity and access the dashboard.
The guide includes a minimal checklist for validating persistence and Excel import/export in production.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor with all logic in backend/main.mo; only add backend/migration.mo if an upgrade migration is necessary.
Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui or any other frontend immutable paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT.
Use English for any user-facing text.
nonGoals: Implementing third-party authentication providers other than Internet Identity.
Adding external databases or non-IC storage systems.
Implementing custom report execution beyond the existing report definition storage unless required for Excel export.
